docs.title: Welcome to MkDocs
docs.text: For full documentation visit mkdocs.org.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• mkdocs new [dir-name] - Create a new project.
  • mkdocs serve - Start the live-reloading docs server.
  • mkdocs build - Build the documentation site.
  • mkdocs -h - Print help message and exit.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
mkdocs.yml    # The configuration file.
docs/
    index.md  # The documentation homepage.
    ...       # Other markdown pages, images and other files.

docs.title: Installing grafana with docker image
docs.text:
Use Docker volumes (recommended)

Use Docker volumes when you want the Docker Engine to manage the storage volume.

To use Docker volumes for persistent storage, complete the following steps:

docs.title: Step 1: Create a project folder, choose any path
docs.text:
mkdir grafana-docker
cd grafana-docker

docs.title: Step 2: Create docker-compose.yml and add this content
docs.text:
services:
    grafana:
        image: grafana/grafana-enterprise
        container_name: grafana
        restart: unless-stopped
        ports:
        - '3000:3000'
        volumes:
        - grafana-storage:/var/lib/grafana
volumes:
    grafana-storage: {}

docs.title: Step 3: Save the file and run the following command:
docs.text: docker compose up -d

docs.title: Stopping the docker
docs.text: docker compose down

docs.title: You need to create github repository before executing the following codes.
MkDocs has a built-in command to push to GitHub Pages:
docs.text:
mkdocs gh-deploy

Your site will be live at:

https://{YOUR_USERNAME}.github.io/my-docs/

Optional settings in mkdocs.yml You can specify your site URL so MkDocs knows the correct path: site_name: My Docs site_url: https://YOUR_USERNAME.github.io/my-docs/

docs.title: Updating your site, Whenever you make changes:
docs.text:
mkdocs build      # optional, just to check locally
mkdocs serve      # optional, preview locally
mkdocs gh-deploy  # push updated site to GitHub Pages

docs.title: Preview locally before deploying
docs.text:
mkdocs serve

Visit: http://127.0.0.1:8000

Make sure all links and nested pages work correctly.

docs.title: n8n docker image with native postgresql
Step 1: Verify PostgreSQL is reachable from Docker(you can do this in pgAdmin)
docs.text:
CREATE DATABASE n8n;
CREATE SCHEMA schema_n8n;
GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA schema_n8n TO postgres;

docs.title: Step 2: Create a project folder, choose any path
docs.text:
mkdir n8n-docker
cd n8n-docker

docs.title: Step 3: Create docker-compose.yml and add this content
docs.text:
services:
n8n:
    image: docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n
    container_name: n8n
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
    - "5678:5678"
    environment:
    - TZ=Asia/Manila
    - GENERIC_TIMEZONE=Asia/Manila

    # n8n settings
    - N8N_ENFORCE_SETTINGS_FILE_PERMISSIONS=true
    - N8N_RUNNERS_ENABLED=true

    # Database (PostgreSQL on host)
    - DB_TYPE=postgresdb
    - DB_POSTGRESDB_HOST=host.docker.internal
    - DB_POSTGRESDB_PORT=5432
    - DB_POSTGRESDB_DATABASE=n8n
    - DB_POSTGRESDB_SCHEMA=schema_n8n
    - DB_POSTGRESDB_USER=postgres
    - DB_POSTGRESDB_PASSWORD=P@ssw0rd!

    volumes:
    - n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n

volumes:
n8n_data:

docs.title: STEP 4: Start n8n
docs.text: docker compose up -d

docs.title: Check logs:
docs.text: docker compose logs -f

docs.title: You should see:
docs.text: n8n ready on 0.0.0.0, port 5678

docs.title: Open browser:
docs.text:
http://localhost:5678

Complete the n8n setup wizard

docs.title: 1. Generating requirements.txt using pip freeze
docs.text:
If you want to create a requirements.txt from your current Python environment: pip freeze > requirements.txt

This will list all installed packages with their versions.

Example output inside requirements.txt: numpy==1.26.0 pandas==2.1.0 requests==2.31.0

docs.title: 2. Installing packages from an existing requirements.txt
docs.text:
If you already have a requirements.txt and want to install everything in it:

pip install -r requirements.txt

This will install all listed packages and their specified versions into your current environment.

docs.title: 3. Checking currently installed packages
docs.text:
If you just want to see what’s installed (without writing to a file):

pip freeze

This outputs all installed packages and versions to the terminal.

docs.title: Creating and accessing virtual environment in python
1. Creating a virtual environment
docs.text: python -m [virtual environment name] venv

docs.title: 2. Accessing the virtual environment
docs.text:
source [virtual environment name]/bin/activate   # Linux / Mac
[virtual environment name]\Scripts\activate      # Windows
